title: How to get the free LEGO Astro Bot set – it's not just tied to PlayStation
summary: The new 40899 Astro Bot gift-with-purchase isn't exclusive to the LEGO PlayStation set – Brick Fanatics rounds up other sets that hit the spending threshold.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO's latest gift-with-purchase, 40899 Astro Bot, had looked set to be tied to 72306 PlayStation, but it turns out any qualifying order over the regional spend threshold can net you the freebie. Thresholds are £135 in the UK, $150 in the US, €150 in Europe, and $254 in Australia.

72306 PlayStation (£139.99 / $179.99 / €159.99) does clear the bar, but so do plenty of other October releases and exclusives. Brick Fanatics highlights 21373 Downton Abbey, 72154 Iconic Trainer Moments: Poké Ball, and 75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer (which also unlocks a separate Darth Vader lightsaber GWP) as single sets that qualify. You can also combine smaller releases – pairing 21371 Wallace & Gromit or 11387 Holiday House with 40874 Santa's Holiday Countdown is one suggested combo to reach the threshold.

The article also points to exclusive, retailer-specific sets and retiring models as other routes to the GWP, alongside a currently separate Star Wars promotion offering double points on selected retiring and UCS Star Wars sets until 7 October.

## Why it matters
Gift-with-purchase promotions are a popular way for builders to pick up bonus models, and knowing the spending threshold applies broadly – not just to one set – gives fans far more flexibility in how they shop this October, especially if they're after Star Wars, Pokémon, or other new autumn releases anyway.

## What to watch next
Watch for confirmation on which exact sets remain in stock as GWP stock is often limited, and keep an eye on the separate Star Wars double points promotion deadline of 7 October.

title: LEGO Ideas Review Grows: Hollow Knight and Firefly Serenity Join the Lineup
summary: Two more fan-designed builds have qualified for LEGO Ideas' third and final review of 2026, including a detailed Hollow Knight: Silksong model and a huge Firefly spaceship.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The third and final LEGO Ideas review of 2026 has added its 22nd and 23rd qualifying projects, according to Brick Fanatics.

First is **Hollow Knight: Silksong – The Kingdom of Pharloom**, designed by RexSqueakyDude. It's a tall, vertically-built model that follows Hornet's journey through the game, using a dark outer shell with colourful interior sections to capture the underground setting. Small details like benches and the Diving Bell are reportedly included.

The second addition is **Firefly SERENITY With Interior** by SmallJokeBook — a large, 2,850-piece recreation of the ship from the cult 2002 sci-fi series Firefly. It's said to feature 25 removable modules for interior access (cockpit, dining area, engine bay and more), plus shuttles, movable engines, a working cargo hatch, and space for minifigures of the full main cast.

Both projects have now qualified for LEGO's official review stage, where LEGO decides which fan designs get turned into real sets. This review round already includes other notable projects such as *The Bollaert-Delelis Stadium* by Mirajane62, which qualified back on 11 September — good news for stadium-build fans keeping an eye on this round.

The article also notes that two previous LEGO Ideas-origin sets, 21371 Wallace & Gromit and 21373 Downton Abbey, have now been officially released.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas qualification is the first real step towards a fan design becoming an official set — it doesn't guarantee a release, but it puts these builds in front of LEGO's decision-makers. For fans of video games, cult TV and stadium models alike, this review round has a genuinely varied mix of projects worth watching.

## What to watch next
The third 2026 review is still accepting new qualifiers, so more projects could be added before the list closes. It's also worth watching for LEGO's eventual announcement of which designs from this round get greenlit for production.

title: Rumour: Three LEGO Star Wars UCS sets tipped for 2027, following the AT-ST's unusual path
summary: Fresh rumours point to a third 2027 UCS release, Anakin's Jedi Interceptor, with last year's AT-ST Walker offering clues about how it might be sold and sized.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to Brick Fanatics, rumours suggest LEGO Star Wars could get three Ultimate Collector Series sets in 2027: 75475 UCS TIE Advanced in May, an unannounced 75484 UCS Anakin's Jedi Interceptor in August, and 75487 UCS Millennium Falcon in October. No piece count or price has surfaced for the rumoured Interceptor yet, so treat this as very early speculation.

The pattern mirrors 2025, when three UCS sets - Jango Fett's Starship, the AT-ST Walker and the Death Star - landed in May, August and October respectively. The AT-ST stood out from typical UCS releases in four ways: it launched outside the usual May/October slots, it was the first time three UCS sets arrived in one year since 2002, it wasn't a LEGO.com exclusive (so it reached retailers like Amazon and discounted faster), and it was the smallest UCS set by piece count since 2012. Brick Fanatics suggests this track record could hint at how a third 2027 UCS set might be handled, perhaps smaller and more widely available rather than a flagship direct-to-consumer release.

## Why it matters
UCS sets are among the most sought-after LEGO Star Wars releases for collectors and display builders, so any hint about a third 2027 set - including where it might sell and how big it could be - is worth watching, even at this early, unconfirmed stage.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for official LEGO confirmation of 75484 UCS Anakin's Jedi Interceptor, along with piece count, price and retail availability details, before treating any of this as certain.

title: LEGO Dragon Ball Icons review: Shenron & Goku set impresses despite repetitive build
summary: Brick Fanatics' review of 11390 Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku praises the set's striking curved dragon design and sturdy build, though notes some repetition and only one minifigure.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has published a review of 11390 Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku, part of the LEGO Dragon Ball Icons line. The set uses 1,764 pieces to recreate the coiled dragon Shenron, plus Goku on his Flying Nimbus and all seven Dragon Balls, standing 32cm tall on display.

According to the review, the model's curved dragon body is cleverly engineered, with most of the figure free-standing and supported only at a handful of points along a stone column base. The reviewer says the build can be lifted and even gently shaken without issue, despite its size and apparent fragility.

The set scored 8/10 overall, with particular praise for the design (9/10) and build experience (9/10). Downsides flagged include a repetitive building process in parts, only one minifigure included despite space for more, and a "plaque-moving feature" that didn't excite the reviewer. Value scored lower at 7/10.

## Why it matters
This marks one of LEGO's first forays into Dragon Ball as a licensed theme, and a strong display centrepiece like this could set the tone for how the wider range is received by fans of the anime and by display-build collectors alike.

## What to watch next
It's worth keeping an eye on how this set performs at retail and whether future Dragon Ball Icons releases address the single-minifigure criticism, especially for a theme with such a large and popular cast of characters.

title: LEGO Star Wars UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer now available, with free lightsaber GWP

bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has officially released 75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer, a huge Ultimate Collector Series set that's now the longest LEGO set ever produced. At 6,130 pieces and over 136cm long, it beats the 2011 classic 10221 Super Star Destroyer for size, and comes packed with greebled surface detailing, multiple engine sections, a tiny command tower, a scaled-down Imperial Star Destroyer, display stands and an info plaque. There's also a bridge diorama build featuring minifigures of Darth Vader, Boba Fett, Dengar, Bossk, IG-88, 4-LOM and Zuckuss.

Alongside the set, LEGO is officially offering a gift with purchase: 40897 Darth Vader's Lightsaber, a brick-built hilt over 23cm long with a display stand, nameplate and hidden red kyber crystal. It's free to LEGO Insiders members who buy 75457 at £649.99 / $799.99 / €749.99, but only until 7 October 2026 or while stocks last.

## Why it matters
This is a milestone release for UCS Star Wars collectors — the biggest physical LEGO set to date and a notable step up from the beloved 2011 original. The time-limited free gift adds extra incentive (and FOMO) for anyone considering the purchase, and as a promotional GWP it's likely to become a sought-after collectible in its own right.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on stock levels for both the main set and the lightsaber GWP, as the promotion is time-limited and could sell out before the 7 October cut-off.

title: LEGO's Longest-Ever Set Wasn't Designed to Beat the Titanic
summary: The new UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer has overtaken the Titanic as LEGO's longest set ever, but its designer says that was never the plan.
bodyMarkdown:

LEGO's new Ultimate Collector Series set, 75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer, measures a whopping 136cm long — just enough to edge out 10294 Titanic as the longest official LEGO set ever released.

Instead, the length came down to part constraints. The engine section was based on an existing model, and the team had limited choices for scaling it — essentially certain Technic wheels or specific brick sizes. Once those fixed points were locked in, the rest of the ship's proportions followed, and the model ended up longer than intended.

In official marketing, LEGO has been careful to describe it as the longest Star Wars model rather than directly claiming the overall longest LEGO set title — even though it does now hold that record.

75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer launches for LEGO Insiders on 1 October, with a wider release on 4 October, priced at £649.99 / €749.99 / $799.99. Buyers who purchase between 1–7 October will get a free 40897 Darth Vader's Lightsaber gift with purchase while stocks last.

For UCS collectors and display builders, this is a genuinely fascinating look behind the curtain — showing how real engineering and part limitations, not marketing targets, can shape a flagship model's final scale.
